scene_description: Topic ideation for a single lesson, a unit or a whole course. Produces course designs with measurable learning goals, complete segments, and a match for the learners and teaching conditions.

questions.question: What is the course subject or topic?
What type of course is it?
What should students be able to do after the lesson? (Be as specific as possible, e.g. perform an operation on their own, explain a concept)
What are the teaching conditions? (Lab, computer room, online tools, teaching aids, class size)
What teaching style do you want?
What is the assessment or evaluation method?
What hard constraints or taboos apply? (e.g. no internet access, must follow a certain curriculum standard, avoid sensitive topics)

skip_logic.description: Adjust the topic based on course type, learners and lesson hours.
rules: If the user picks "lab / hands-on session", ask about equipment, materials and safety conditions; exclude lab designs with no equipment to support them

If the user picks "primary school students" or "secondary school students", exclude content above their cognitive level, add concrete examples and interaction, and lower the information density accordingly
If the user picks "single lesson" or "one-off workshop", output only that lesson's design, not a full semester outline
If the user picks "fun and interactive" for a theory lecture, humor and games must serve the learning goal; note in the risk warnings that they must not overshadow the content
If the user picks "online course", add online interaction and assignment design; note in the risk warnings the issues of self-discipline and completion rate

tone_examples: Good: By the end of this lesson, students can explain the concept in their own words and correctly identify its two forms in a given case.
Good: The lab segment runs in pairs; each pair must complete the safety checklist before operating, and the teacher confirms power-on.
Bad: This lesson is just for fun, having a good time matters most, it does not matter what you learn.
Bad: There are a lot of points, I will try to cover them all, read the rest on your own.
conditional_notes: When the teaching style is "fun and interactive", gamified design and light language are allowed, but every segment must map to a clear learning goal.
For younger learners, the language can be warmer, but the teaching logic and safety requirements must not be loosened.

constraint_list: There must be clear, measurable learning goals
Content and activities must match the learners' cognitive level
The lesson must have complete segments: warm-up, new material, practice, feedback, wrap-up
There must be a workable assessment or evaluation method
The design must fit the lesson hours, class size and teaching resources
It must follow curriculum standards, the syllabus and safety rules
exclusion_rules: Content overload beyond the lesson's capacity
Lab designs with no lab conditions to support them
Goals the learners cannot actually reach
Practice segments with safety or compliance risks
One-way lecturing with no interaction and no feedback
Taboos the user explicitly lists in constraints_excludes
